title: Sharp Minimax Constants for Optimal Policy Value with Categorical Covariates and Null Cells
banked_reason: Exact leading constant and causal-to-Gaussian transfer remain open; D0.5 graded the sound bracket incremental below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The advertised exact leading constant is not determined: the note proves only a positive finite bracket whose upper side is inherited from the accepted rate result and whose explicit lower constant is not shown sharp. The finite-sample class identity and null-cell closure do not strengthen the already known minimax order, while the endpoint factor 1/3 remains an oracle cusp calculation rather than a causal minimax constant. The certificate theorem supplies an enclosure framework and a loose d=2 regression test, but no growing-dimensional certified computation that closes the scalar gap, demonstrates oscillation, or materially narrows the causal bracket. Both the scalar closure and the uniform observable causal-to-Gaussian transfer are left open, so the package is setup for the headline problem rather than its solution. The framing is largely faithful about these gaps, but the absence of an exact or substantially tightened endpoint characterization limits the projected paper score.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 established an exact observed-table class mapping, null-cell closure, endpoint cusp geometry, a lawful anchored lower bound, and a positive finite normalized-risk bracket. The attempted growing-window scalar closure and two-way unknown-nuisance causal-to-Gaussian risk transfer were not proved; the exact leading constant, observable sharp estimator, and matching priors remain open. D0.5 graded the sound result incremental, below the field floor.
tldr: For the null-cell-permitting optimal-value model at overlap \(1/4\), the present decision problem is exactly the accepted all-alphabet observed-law problem for every finite \(n,d\), and its positive-mass and null-cell minimax risks coincide. Along every stated nonsaturated sequence, the common normalized liminf and limsup have a proved positive finite bracket, with explicit anchored lower constant \(\beta_*^2/(3\mathrm e^2)\) and the accepted Jackson--factorial upper comparison constant. The endpoint tie calculation gives the leading oracle cusp factor \(1/3\), but equality with the sequence-specific growing-window Gaussian endpoints remains an open risk-transfer problem. The rational finite programs and global tail envelopes provide certified scalar enclosures without importing the fixed-window Bernstein constant.
gap: The closest causal theorem determines only the rate \(d/(n\log d)\) for an all-alphabet problem and leaves convergence of the sharp overlap-dependent normalization open, while the closest exact Gaussian theorem assumes a fixed standardized bound. No checked source characterizes the causal liminf and limsup over a null-cell-permitting nonsaturated sequence class or supplies finite-dimensional certified errors together with globally valid tail envelopes capable of deciding equality, oscillation, or nonclosure.
fill: The project proves exact positive-mass closure and a causal-to-Gaussian liminf and limsup factorization for every sequence satisfying \(d_n(\log d_n)^{20}/n\to0\), constructs an observable estimator and matching all-estimator priors, and reduces the earlier all-\(d\) sharp-overlap question on this branch to Gaussian scalar closure. Fixed rational grids, hat sieves, exact-mixture denominators, outward Taylor and Gaussian-tail arithmetic, and global solver gaps produce checkable block endpoints \(L_J\) and \(U_J\). The uniform envelopes \(C_J^-\) and \(C_J^+\) certify a common limit only when their whole-tail gap vanishes; the high--low envelopes \(H_J^-\) and \(H_J^+\) certify oscillation when strictly separated, and otherwise expose nonclosure.
